title: The Wolf of Ashvale Revisited
premise: Emrys Nystrom, a memory-thief hiding in the magic-outlawed city of Ashvale, is found by a child named Vess who speaks the First Tongue and carries a fragment of a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain. The child's soul belongs to Emrys's long-dead sister, whose death twelve years ago was no accident but a bargain struck by the magistrates who outlawed magic to hoard it for themselves. As dragon-fire—the last living magic—gutters beneath the mountain, Emrys must gather her old criminal family, betray and be betrayed by the man she loves, and descend into the court of the dead to steal back what was sold. She succeeds at terrible cost: she trades her own memories of her sister to complete the soul, giving Vess a whole life while Emrys chooses to forget the person who made her who she is.
about_author: Ines Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive institutions by refusing to be remembered by them.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hours
chapters.summary: Emrys works her stall in Ashvale's night market, selling stolen memories disguised as luck-charms while dodging the Wardens who enforce the magic ban. A routine theft from a dying magistrate reveals an official seal bearing her sister's name. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: weary competence shadowed by an old grief she refuses to name.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Dead Hour
chapters.summary: A child appears at Emrys's door speaking a language older than any kingdom—a language Emrys recognizes because it was their childhood secret. The child, Vess, carries a locket containing a sliver of glowing soul-light. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror curdling into recognition; the past has found her address.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Wardens raid the night market hunting the child's 'anomalous speech.' Emrys hides Vess among her charms and watches her neighbor, a fence named Osk, taken in her place. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: guilt—the invisibility she bought with silence now costs other people.

chapters.title: The Locket's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys reads the locket's memory-imprint and learns the truth: her sister Bryn's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain by the magistrates themselves, and Vess is the vessel they used to carry the payment. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: cold fury replacing grief; the law is the crime.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Emrys and Bryn learning the First Tongue, the fire that killed Bryn, and the bargain Emrys made to forget enough to survive. POV: Emrys (past). Emotional beat: tenderness and self-betrayal; she remembers choosing not to remember.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept Her Secrets
chapters.summary: Emrys turns to Corvane, a Warden captain she has loved and lied to for years, believing he can get them out of the city. He agrees—but she sees him pocket one of her charms. POV: alternating Emrys/Corvane. Emotional beat: love strained by the suspicion that loyalty has a price tag.

chapters.title: Down Among the Unlicensed
chapters.summary: Emrys seeks her old crew: Sefa the lockwitch, the twins Pell and Rook, all living half-lives under false names. They refuse until Vess speaks the First Tongue and each hears a dead relative's voice in it. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: reluctant hope; old loyalty rekindling against everyone's judgment.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: The crew needs a map of the mountain's undercourt, held by a memory-broker called the Tithe. He demands payment in Emrys's happiest memory. She pays—and immediately feels the hole where it was. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: dread; she is spending herself to save her sister, just as she did before.

chapters.title: Ashvale Closes Its Gates
chapters.summary: Corvane seals the city gates to trap the thieves, then privately warns Emrys to flee alone—he claims he's protecting her. Vess overhears and calls him a liar in the First Tongue. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: his genuine love revealed as its own kind of cage.

chapters.title: The Guttering Light
chapters.summary: Beneath the mountain, the last dragon-fire dims; when it dies, every soul in the court becomes permanent property of the magistrates. The crew descends through flooded mine-shafts as the deadline becomes real. POV: Rook. Emotional beat: ticking-clock urgency mixed with awe at the dying wonder below.

chapters.title: Court of Sold Souls
chapters.summary: The undercourt revealed: rows of souls shelved like inventory, tended by clerks who were once thieves who took this same road. Sefa finds her brother's shelf and falters. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: horror domesticated into bureaucracy; evil as paperwork.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: A head clerk offers Emrys a trade: Bryn's soul for Vess's body as a new vessel. Emrys refuses, learning the sale requires a willing blood-kin signature—hers, forged twelve years ago. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: devastation; she has been the instrument of her sister's imprisonment all along.

chapters.title: What Corvane Carried Down
chapters.summary: Corvane arrives with Wardens—but he has spent years secretly returning confiscated memories, and he offers the crew his evidence against the magistrates instead of arrest. His superior executes him on the spot. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: tragic redemption; loyalty finally aligned with truth, too late to enjoy it.

chapters.title: Riot of the Shelved
chapters.summary: Emrys releases fragments of stolen memory into the court, and the shelved souls remember who they were, rising against the clerks. In the chaos the crew fights toward Bryn's shelf. POV: Pell. Emotional beat: exhilaration and chaos; justice outside the law looks like a riot.

chapters.title: The Signature in Her Hand
chapters.summary: At Bryn's shelf, Emrys discovers the forged signature can be unmade only by a kin's true hand—meaning she must sign the release and accept whatever debt follows. She signs. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grim resolve; claiming authorship of her worst act to undo it.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire, One Breath Left
chapters.summary: The magistrates flood the court to smother the rebellion and the dragon-fire together. Vess, hearing Bryn's voice for the first time, walks toward the flame instead of away. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: heartbreaking agency; the child chooses the fire that made her.

chapters.title: The Trade Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: To make Bryn's soul whole, something of equal love must fill the hollow. Emrys offers every memory of Bryn—all twelve years of grief and all the childhood before it. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax; she saves her sister by erasing the reason she came.

chapters.title: Sister, Stranger
chapters.summary: Bryn's soul rises whole into Vess, who wakes carrying two lifetimes. Emrys looks at them both and feels nothing—no grief, no recognition, only a stranger's kindness. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: bittersweet reunion witnessed by the one person who can't feel it.

chapters.title: The Mountain Exhales
chapters.summary: The freed souls escape as the dragon-fire flares once more and gutters out forever, taking the magistrates' hoarded magic with it. Above, Ashvale's wards fail and the ban collapses. POV: Rook. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph; the world changes because a few thieves refused the ledger.

chapters.title: Trials Nobody Presided Over
chapters.summary: The surviving magistrates face the crowd, not a court. Sefa chooses mercy over execution, arguing that becoming the ledger would prove the ledgers right. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: hard-won principle; justice without vengeance is harder and better.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hours, Again
chapters.summary: Emrys reopens her stall, unable to say why she keeps a child's wooden bird among her wares or why certain songs make her weep. Vess visits daily, telling her stories of a woman named Bryn. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: quiet ache; identity persisting beyond memory.

chapters.title: First Tongue
chapters.summary: Vess teaches Emrys the language she no longer knows she knew, word by word, and in the final lesson says 'sister.' Something in Emrys answers before her mind can object. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: resolution without restoration; love rebuilding itself from scratch, and choosing to stay.
